name: Report results to clinicians and long-term care homes
summary: Once laboratory results are verified, the LIS builds a cumulative report for each requisition and sends interim and final versions to the ordering clinician and copy-to recipients by EMR batch download, the eResults web portal, auto-fax or printed copies carried by courier, submits Ontario results to the provincial laboratory information system, and queues the order for billing and the patient portal. Almost all of this is automatic. People work the exceptions: unmatched providers, failed faxes and interface errors, report copy requests, amended reports after an error is found, and misdirected reports that become privacy incidents. Elapsed time is set mainly by the slowest test on the requisition and by EMR download and courier schedules.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company reporting about 690,000 community requisitions a month from regional laboratories to clinics, LTC homes and the provincial repository.
baseline.notes: One case is one final report for a requisition, from the first verified result to delivery of the final report, plus copy requests. Critical result calls are a separate process.

trigger: A result on a community requisition is verified by autoverification or a technologist, or the contact centre logs a request for a copy of a report.
end_state: The final report (and any interim reports) has reached every recipient by their delivery channel and OLIS, the order is queued for billing and the portal, or an amended report or copy has been sent, or a misdirected report has been contained and passed to the privacy office.

volume.seasonality: Follows requisition volume: lower in summer and late December, higher January to March and in the autumn; weekday heavy.

evidence.note: One final report per community requisition, from the organisation file demand driver d_community_reqs; seasonality is the author's estimate.

Cost from the organisation file (Job Bank NOC 33101 times 1.35). About 15 of the 150 processing assistants work the reporting desk (print and courier bundles, fax failures, unknown providers, copy requests); author's estimate.
HL7, EMR batch and OLIS interfaces described; about two of the twelve interface analysts work result delivery errors; author's estimate.

roles.title: Charge technologist
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Amended report investigations and privacy incident logging; author's estimate within the 28 charge technologists in the organisation file.

roles.title: Laboratory medical director or clinical scientist (clinical pathologist, biochemist, microbiologist)
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: Review of clinically significant amendments; author's estimate.

systems.name: Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Interface engine for HL7 orders and results with EMRs and hospital LIS
eResults provider portal and EMR results delivery
Laboratory billing and accounts receivable system (provincial claims, patient, client invoices)
CRM for client accounts, sales pipeline and service cases
Quality management system software (document control, CAPA, training records)

steps.name: Receive a reporting trigger
steps.description: The LIS registers either a newly verified result on a requisition (from the core, microbiology, cytology, pathology or reference laboratory) or a report copy request logged by the contact centre, and starts the matching reporting path.

evidence.note: Split of triggers is the author's estimate; copy requests come from the contact centre process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Assemble the cumulative report and check completeness
steps.description: The LIS builds the cumulative report for the requisition with reference ranges, flags, interpretive and specimen comments and any critical call note, and checks whether every ordered test is final.

error.defect_description: Report template or comment mapping error.

next.condition: all tests on the requisition are final
some tests still pending (culture, cytology, reference or send-out)

evidence.note: Interference comments shown in place of a number follow r_krasowski. Share of requisitions with pending tests at first release is the author's estimate (about 16% of requisitions include microbiology, cytology or referred tests by the organisation file volumes).

steps.name: Release an interim report
steps.description: The LIS sends an interim report with the completed results marked final and the rest marked pending, through the same delivery channels as a final report.

evidence.note: Interim and final cumulative reports are described in the organisation file process map; timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hold until the last pending result is verified
steps.description: The requisition waits in the LIS until the slowest test (for example a urine culture, Pap test or referred specialised test) is verified; nobody works on the report while it waits.

evidence.note: Cultures take one to three days and cytology or referred tests up to a week or more; author's estimate.

steps.name: Apply recipient, delivery and suppression rules
steps.description: The LIS looks up the ordering provider and copy-to recipients on the requisition, their client account and each one's delivery preference (EMR batch, eResults web, auto-fax or printed copy), and applies rules such as withholding sensitive results from the portal.

error.defect_description: Copy-to recipient mapped to the wrong account.

next.condition: every recipient matched to an account
ordering or copy-to provider not found or inactive

evidence.note: Delivery options from r_eresults and r_hcp; the unmatched-provider share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Resolve an unknown or unmatched provider
steps.description: A reporting assistant opens the requisition image, searches the provider registry and client accounts for the name and billing number, phones the clinic if needed, links the correct provider in the LIS and requests a new client account when there is none.

error.defect_description: Report linked to a provider with a similar name.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; queue worked during the day shift.

steps.name: Queue the billable order and portal release
steps.description: The LIS sends the completed order with test codes and payer to the billing system and queues the results for the patient portal under its release rules; no one touches this step.

evidence.note: Hand-offs to provincial billing and the portal are in the organisation file process map.

steps.name: Submit Ontario results to OLIS
steps.description: The interface engine sends results on Ontario requisitions to the provincial laboratory information system so that other authorized clinicians can see them; Quebec and Manitoba reports skip this step. The engine then sends the report down the recipient's delivery channel.

control.basis: Provincial requirement for community laboratories to contribute results to OLIS (Ontario)

next.condition: recipient takes EMR or eResults delivery
recipient takes printed reports (some LTC homes and small clinics)

evidence.note: Community laboratories contribute to OLIS (r_olis, r_olis_lab). The legal basis is the author's understanding and was not confirmed in an opened source. Channel shares are the author's estimates for 2019-2022.

steps.name: Correct an OLIS rejection
steps.description: An interface analyst reads the rejection acknowledgement (for example an unmapped test code, invalid health card format or missing provider identifier), corrects the data or the code mapping and resubmits the message.

error.defect_description: Mapping fix introduces a new error for another test.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; errors are often worked in groups after one mapping fix.

steps.name: Deliver to the clinician's EMR or eResults inbox
steps.description: The report is posted to eResults and, for EMR users, made available to the practice's EMR batch download in the company's conformance format; the EMR collects new results on its own schedule.

next.condition: an error in the released report is found later

evidence.note: EMR batch service from r_eresults; the batch interval and error shares are the author's estimate. The later-error branch stands for amended reports, about 0.1% of reports (author's estimate).

steps.name: Send the report by auto-fax
steps.description: The fax server sends the report to the clinic's fax number on file, retrying busy lines automatically; Level II alert results are timed for 08:00 to 20:00.

error.defect_description: Report faxed to a wrong or outdated number.

next.condition: an error in the released report is found later

evidence.note: Fax delivery and Level II timing from r_oaml and r_alpha; failure and misdirection shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Work the failed electronic delivery queue
steps.description: An interface analyst reviews messages with errors or missing acknowledgements, checks the EMR connection and provider mapping with the clinic's vendor, and resends or switches the clinic to fax until the connection is fixed.

error.defect_description: Resend duplicates reports in the EMR.

evidence.note: Interface outages affect many messages at once, so per-report time is small; author's estimate.

steps.name: Follow up a failed fax
steps.description: A reporting assistant checks the number against the client account, phones the clinic to confirm the fax line or a new number, updates the account and re-faxes, or switches the report to printed delivery.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Print, sort and bundle reports for courier delivery
steps.description: A reporting assistant prints reports in batches by courier route, checks the page count and recipient on each, puts them in sealed envelopes and adds them to the route bags.

error.defect_description: Report put in the wrong envelope.

evidence.note: Print batches timed to courier routes; author's estimate.

steps.name: Courier delivers the printed report
steps.description: The company courier carries the bundle on the next scheduled route to the clinic or long-term care home, where staff file it in the resident or patient chart.

next.condition: an error in the released report is found later

evidence.note: Next-route delivery, longer over weekends; author's estimate.

steps.name: Investigate the error and enter the corrected result
steps.description: After a clinician query, a QC look-back or an internal review finds an error in a released report (wrong result, wrong patient, wrong units or comment), the charge technologist confirms it against the instrument record and specimen, opens a nonconformance, and enters the corrected result in the LIS with an amended flag and the reason.

control.basis: ISO 15189 revised reports: amended reports clearly identified with the reason, original retained; CLSI C24 corrected reports

next.condition: change the clinician should hear about now

evidence.note: Corrected report practice from r_clp_c24; the delay until discovery and the shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Medical director reviews a significant amendment
steps.description: The medical director reviews the error, the corrected value and its clinical impact, approves the amended report wording and decides whether the clinician must be phoned.

control.basis: ISO 15189 laboratory director responsibility for reports; laboratory amended report procedure

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Phone the ordering clinician about the corrected result
steps.description: The charge technologist calls the clinician's office, explains the original and corrected values, records who was told and when, and adds a call note to the amended report.

control.basis: CLSI C24 and laboratory procedure: providers are told when a corrected report is issued

evidence.note: Provider notification from r_clp_c24; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Re-send the amended report to all recipients and OLIS
steps.description: The LIS sends the amended report, marked as corrected, to every original recipient and to OLIS through the same channels, and updates the portal copy.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Retrieve a misdirected report and send it correctly
steps.description: A reporting assistant takes the call from the clinic that received the wrong report, asks them to destroy or return it and confirm in writing, identifies the cause (wrong number, similar provider name, envelope error) and sends the report to the right recipient.

control.basis: Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004 (Ontario): reasonable steps to contain a privacy breach

evidence.note: Confidentiality duty from r_csmls; PHIPA basis and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Log the privacy incident and notify the privacy office
steps.description: The charge technologist records the incident with the patient, recipient, cause and containment in the quality system and sends it to the privacy office, which decides on patient notification and reporting to the commissioner.

control.basis: Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004: breach notification to the individual and, where thresholds are met, the Information and Privacy Commissioner

evidence.note: Hand-off to the privacy incident process is in the organisation file; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Verify a copy request and the requester's authority
steps.description: A reporting assistant opens the request from the contact centre, checks that the requester is the ordering clinician's office, a named copy-to clinician or another authorized custodian, and confirms patient identity and the report wanted; patients asking for their own records are directed to the portal or a records request.

error.defect_description: Copy sent to a clinician without authority.

control.basis: Personal Health Information Protection Act, 2004: disclosure only to authorized recipients

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Retrieve and re-send the report copy
steps.description: The assistant retrieves the final report in the LIS, adds the new recipient as a copy-to where allowed, and faxes or posts it to eResults, noting the disclosure in the request record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Pending tests
exceptions.description: A culture, cytology, referred or send-out test is still pending, so an interim report goes out first and the final report waits for the last result.

exceptions.name: Unknown or unmatched provider
exceptions.description: The ordering or copy-to provider is not on file or inactive; the report waits until an assistant identifies the provider and links the account.

exceptions.name: Failed fax
exceptions.description: A fax fails after retries; an assistant confirms the number with the clinic and re-faxes or switches to printed delivery.

exceptions.name: Interface or OLIS error
exceptions.description: An EMR delivery or OLIS message is rejected or not acknowledged and is fixed and resent by an interface analyst.

exceptions.name: Amended report
exceptions.description: An error in a released report is found later; the result is corrected with an amended flag, reviewed by the medical director when significant, phoned to the clinician and re-sent to all recipients and OLIS.

exceptions.name: Misdirected report
exceptions.description: A report reaches the wrong clinic; it is retrieved, sent correctly and logged as a privacy incident.

exceptions.name: Copy request
exceptions.description: A clinic or authorized custodian asks for a copy or redirect; an assistant checks authority and re-sends.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the first verified result on a requisition to delivery of the final report
benchmarks.population: Community requisitions in a large Ontario community laboratory

evidence.note: Author's estimate: electronic reports are available as soon as results are verified (r_eresults) and collected on the EMR's batch schedule, so most final reports arrive within about two hours; requisitions with cultures, cytology or referred tests wait days. Consistent with the 24-hour routine result target (r_ag2017).

benchmarks.unit: percent of routine blood and chemistry tests, 2016/17

evidence.note: End-to-end measure that includes reporting.

benchmarks.population: Ontario community laboratories following the OAML guideline

pain_points.description: Clinics without a working EMR interface depend on fax and printed reports, which fail more often, need follow-up calls and carry most of the misdirection risk.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Final reports for mixed requisitions wait for the slowest test, so clinicians receive several interim versions and can act on incomplete reports.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Unmatched or inactive providers stop delivery until someone identifies the clinician from the requisition image.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Amended reports take a charge technologist's investigation, sometimes a medical director's review and a phone call, and must reach every recipient and OLIS again.

sources.title: eResults
sources.supports: Free online results service for providers and corporate clients: batch service loads results into EMRs that meet the company's conformance standards; online service for web viewing and printing; HL7 and ACORD interfaces; results available as soon as they are available.

sources.title: Healthcare provider solutions
sources.supports: Results through the clinician's EMR or EHR and through the free eResults service; links to the OAML test reporting guideline.

sources.title: Ontario Laboratories Information System (OLIS)
sources.supports: OLIS gives authorized providers lab orders and results from hospitals, public health and community laboratories on one platform and can feed EMRs.

sources.title: Lab results
sources.supports: OLIS holds orders and results from hospitals, community labs and public health labs; clinicians with OntarioMD-certified EMRs view OLIS results in the EMR; capable of storing more than 68,000 test result types.

sources.title: 2017 Annual Report, Section 3.07: Laboratory Services in the Health Sector
sources.publisher: Office of the Auditor General of Ontario
sources.supports: Community laboratories target routine blood and chemistry results within 24 hours of pickup; two providers met it for 94% and 99% of tests in 2016/17; laboratories send results back to the ordering health-care professional.

sources.title: Guideline for Reporting Laboratory Test Results (CLP-025), revised September 2009
sources.publisher: Ontario Association of Medical Laboratories (copy hosted by the model laboratory)
sources.supports: Level II alert results are faxed or phoned 08:00 to 20:00 and attempts stop once results are delivered routinely (electronic, fax or hard copy); ASAP results are communicated by fax or other electronic means, most in under 24 hours; clinicians may direct Level II results to electronic delivery.

sources.title: Test reporting
sources.supports: Peer Ontario community laboratory: urgent results about 3 hours from receipt; ASAP routine tests communicated within 24 hours by fax or telephone; Level II alerts phoned or faxed 08:00 to 24:00.

sources.title: The 7 best practices to recover from an out-of-control event
sources.supports: When re-analysis shows differences beyond the laboratory director's limits, corrected reports are issued promptly and providers are told a corrected report has been issued.

sources.title: Autoverification in a core clinical chemistry laboratory at an academic medical center (Krasowski et al.)
sources.supports: Results exceeding interference limits are reported as haemolysed, lipaemic or icteric instead of a number and charges are credited; clinicians must request an override.

sources.title: Standards of practice
sources.publisher: Canadian Society for Medical Laboratory Science
sources.supports: Laboratory professionals document, protect and maintain confidential information and verify relevant data.

sources.title: Wages: Medical Laboratory Technical Assistant in Ontario (NOC 33101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $17.95, median $26.25, high $36.00 (2023-2024).

sources.title: Hospital solutions
sources.supports: Bi-directional order and result interfaces with hospital LIS systems (Meditech, SCC Soft, QuadraMed, Sunquest); nine laboratories; more than 500 hospitals.

assumptions: One case is one final report per requisition; interim reports are part of the same case. Copy requests (about 2%) enter through the same first step.
Delivery channel shares for 2019-2022 are the author's estimates: about 78% EMR or eResults, 17% auto-fax and 5% printed copies.
OLIS submission is modelled for Ontario reports. The organisation file has no external party for OLIS, so the submission is described inside the process and not listed in interfaces.produces.
The legal basis for OLIS contribution was not confirmed in an opened source; it is marked fixed_by_law on the author's understanding of Ontario requirements for licensed community laboratories.

Patient portal and billing hand-offs happen for every final report in the model (outcome any); the portal process applies its own registration and release rules, so only registered patients see results.
The amended report rate (about 0.1% of reports) and the misdirected report rate (about 5 per 100,000) are the author's estimates; no opened source gave rates.
The notification_record and lis_change inputs from the process map are enabling inputs (call notes printed on reports, configuration changes), so they carry a share of 0.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
